prompt.brief: Design an explainable churn-prediction platform that builds leakage-resistant customer features, scores risk ahead of renewal, identifies drivers, and feeds measurable retention campaigns.
successSignals: Define customer identity, churn labels, observation/prediction windows, point-in-time features, segment policies, model versions, and attribution.
Prevent target leakage and bias, handle censoring and delayed outcomes, calibrate probabilities, and expose confidence and data freshness.
Separate batch training/scoring from online lookups and campaign delivery; make scores reproducible, idempotent, and rollbackable.
Explain privacy, retention, explainability, drift, human overrides, experiment measurement, observability, and stale-score fallback.

functional: Ingest customer events and outcomes, create point-in-time features, train/evaluate models, publish approved scores, and calculate drivers.
Query customer and segment risk with model version/freshness/confidence, export eligible audiences, and record campaign treatment/outcome.
Support score correction, customer deletion, model rollback, retraining, bias/performance monitoring, and campaign deduplication.
nonFunctional: Publish a calibrated score at least 30 days before the prediction horizon with documented precision/recall and freshness.
Score 100M customers and serve analyst dashboards without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100M customers, weekly scoring, and 10k analyst dashboard users
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Explainable churn-prediction platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Explainable churn-prediction platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Explainable churn-prediction platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Explainable churn-prediction platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Explainable churn-prediction platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Explainable churn-prediction platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Explainable churn-prediction platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Explainable churn-prediction platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Explainable churn-prediction platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
